candidates.angle: duḥhalayam, the abode of suffering, as a temporary home
mahātmānaḥ, great souls, having reached supreme fulfillment
mamam, me, the safe destination beyond the cycle of birth

angle_en: Dhuhalayama: the temporary home of pain

en.intro: Krishna continues by naming the destination that lies beyond the cycle of birth, a place where suffering ends.
en.notice: The word dhuhalayama, abode of suffering, describes this world of rebirth, and the verse tells us that those who reach Krishna do not return to it.
en.next: Krishna then speaks of all worlds returning to this same cycle, except for the one who reaches him.
en.meaning: Great souls who reach me do not return to this painful, temporary cycle of birth.

hi.intro: कृष्ण आगे उस मंजिल का नाम लेते हैं जो जन्म के चक्र से परे है, जहाँ दुख का अंत होता है।
hi.meaning: महात्मा, जो मुझे प्राप्त करके परमसिद्धि को पहुँच गए हैं, वे इस दुःखालय और अशाश्वत पुनर्जन्म को प्राप्त नहीं होते।
hi.notice: यहाँ दुःखालयम् का अर्थ है दुःख का घर, यह संसार। जो मुझे पा लेते हैं, वे इस दुःख के घर में वापस नहीं आते।
hi.next: ब्रह्मा के लोक तक के सभी संसार वापस लौट आते हैं, पर जो मुझे पा लेते हैं, उनका पुनर्जन्म नहीं होता।

en.intro: Krishna continues by naming the destination that lies beyond the cycle of birth, a place where suffering ends.
en.body: Great souls who reach me do not return to this painful, temporary cycle of birth. The word dhuhalayama, abode of suffering, describes this world of rebirth, and the verse tells us that those who reach Krishna do not return to it. Krishna then speaks of all worlds returning to this same cycle, except for the one who reaches him.

issues: unsupported: "अर्थात् उनको परम प्रेमकी प्राप्ति हो गयी है" (The source text and its standard translation do not mention 'परम प्रेम' (supreme love). The verse states that great souls have reached 'परमसिद्धि' (supreme fulfillment) or 'संसिद्धिम् परमाम्' (supreme perfection), not supreme love.)

borrowed: "कृष्ण कहते हैं कि ब्रह्मा के लोक तक सब लौट आते हैं" (This phrase is taken directly from the NEXT verse (8.16), which states 'ब्रह्माप्तिम लोकं तूप्यन्यं पुनरावर्तिनोऽर्जुन' and 'ब्रह्माप्तिम लोकं तूप्यन्यं'. It is incorrectly presented as part of the current verse's content.)

unsupported: "अर्थात् उनको परम प्रेमकी प्राप्ति हो गयी है" (The source verse and its standard translations focus on reaching 'supreme perfection' (paramaṁ siddhiṁ) and escaping the cycle of birth. The phrase 'attainment of supreme love' (parama prem) is a specific theological interpretation not found in the provided source text.)

meaning_changed: "अर्थात् उनको परम प्रेमकी प्राप्ति हो गयी है" (The source and fixed meaning state that great souls do not return to the cycle of birth because they have attained supreme fulfillment (samsiddhim paramam). The Hindi translation adds an unsupported etymological and theological interpretation that 'paramasiddhi' means 'param prem' (supreme love), which changes the meaning from supreme fulfillment to supreme love.)
